overview:
The desert doesn't have to mean roughing it. This four-day private trip from Marrakech takes you to the great dunes of the Erg Chebbi with every night chosen for comfort and character: a restored earthen kasbah in the Dades valley, a hotel with a pool at the foot of the dunes, and a luxury camp in the sand, where each tent has a king-size bed, proper linen and its own bathroom with a hot shower. You travel in a comfortable 4x4 with your own driver, at an unhurried pace, with time for long lunches, photo stops and the pool.

Most 4-day desert tours rush to the dunes and back with a single night in a basic camp. We spend two nights at Merzouga instead – one in a hotel by the dunes and one in the camp – so you have a full day to explore the desert by 4x4, visit a nomad family, hear Gnawa music in Khamlia and rest before the camel ride at sunset. Along the way you see the highlights of the south: the Tichka pass, the UNESCO ksar of Ait Ben Haddou with a local guide, the Skoura palm grove, the rose valley, the Dades and the Todra gorges.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: 4 days, 3 nights
• Start and finish: Marrakech (or end in Fes on request)
• Nights: boutique kasbah hotel in the Dades, hotel with pool in Merzouga, luxury desert camp
• Type: private tour with your own driver in a 4x4
• Meals: dinner and breakfast every night; lunches free so you choose where to eat
• Activity level: easy; a short camel ride and gentle walks
• Longest drive: Day 4, about 10 hours with stops back to Marrakech

WHAT MAKES IT LUXURY
• Luxury camp tents with king-size or twin beds, quality linen, rugs, electric light and an en-suite bathroom with hot shower and flush toilet.
• Character hotels: a kasbah of earth and palm wood with a terrace over the valley; a hotel with a pool facing the Erg Chebbi.
• A full private day in the desert by 4x4 instead of a quick drop at the camp.
• Private service throughout: no shared minibuses, no fixed timetable, special touches for honeymoons and anniversaries on request.

WHO WILL ENJOY IT
Couples and honeymooners, families who want comfort for children, travellers who have done basic camps before and want something better, and anyone who would rather spend two nights at the dunes than rush.

WHO MIGHT PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
Couples on a shorter schedule may prefer the [romantic 3-day Merzouga trip](/en-US/morocco/marrakech/tours/romantic-3-day-merzouga-desert-trip-from-marrakech-for-couples-honeymooners/31d06c73cf6cf329225762a3). For a more classic version with two nights at Merzouga, see the [4-day Marrakech to Merzouga desert adventure](/en-US/morocco/marrakech/tours/4-day-marrakech-to-merzouga-desert-adventure-including-2-nights-in-merzouga/685bc9fed3965e7948ffb7d3).

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Dress codes are relaxed. Bring a warm layer for desert evenings (nights can drop close to 0°C from December to February), swimwear for the pool from April to October, a scarf and sunglasses against sand and sun, and a small bag for the camp night – your main luggage stays in the 4x4. Some luxury camps serve wine and beer; ask us if this matters to you.
descriptions:
What to expect: a scenic drive over the High Atlas to the kasbahs of the south, a guided visit of Ait Ben Haddou and your first night in a boutique kasbah hotel above the Dades valley.

Your driver picks you up at your riad or hotel in Marrakech in the morning. The road climbs through the Berber villages and walnut groves of the High Atlas to the Tizi n'Tichka pass at 2,260 m, with stops for photos and a coffee on the way. On the southern side, the landscape turns dry, red and wide open.

At Ait Ben Haddou, the fortified village of earthen houses listed by UNESCO in 1987 and used as a film set from Lawrence of Arabia to Gladiator, a local guide walks you up through the lanes to the old granary at the top. Lunch is at a kasbah restaurant with a view. In the afternoon you pass Ouarzazate and continue along the road of the kasbahs: the Skoura palm grove, the rose valley of Kelaat M'Gouna, and finally the Dades valley. Your hotel is a restored kasbah of earth and palm wood with a terrace over the valley, where dinner is served when the weather allows.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
08:00 – Pick-up at your riad or hotel in Marrakech.
10:00 – Tizi n'Tichka pass and photo stops.
11:30 – Ait Ben Haddou with a local guide (about 1.5 hours).
13:00 – Lunch at a kasbah restaurant (not included).
15:00 – Ouarzazate and the Skoura palm grove.
16:30 – Kelaat M'Gouna, the valley of roses.
18:00 – Arrival at your boutique kasbah hotel; dinner.

GOOD TO KNOW
• About 330 km and 8–9 hours with stops; the road over the Atlas is winding.
• In May the rose valley holds its rose festival; in spring the fields are in flower.
• The pass can be cold and windy even when Marrakech is warm.

INCLUDED: private 4x4 and driver, local guide at Ait Ben Haddou, boutique kasbah hotel with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

PHOTO SPOTS
• Ait Ben Haddou from across the river.
• The kasbahs of Skoura among the palms.
• Sunset on the red cliffs from your hotel terrace.

Overnight: boutique kasbah hotel in the Dades valley.
Meals: dinner.

What to expect: a short morning in the Dades gorge, a walk in the Todra Gorge and an afternoon by the pool at a hotel facing the dunes.

After breakfast on the terrace, your driver takes you a little way up the Dades gorge to see the famous hairpin road and the rock formations known as the monkey fingers. Then you head east to Tinghir and the Todra Gorge, where limestone walls up to 300 m high close in to about 10 m apart above a clear stream. You walk through the narrowest section, with time for photos and a mint tea.

The road then crosses the desert plains past Tinejdad and its old khettara water channels to Erfoud, where you can see how the black fossil marble of the region is cut and polished. In the late afternoon the Erg Chebbi appears on the horizon. Your hotel stands at the foot of the dunes, with a pool and a terrace facing the sand: the perfect place to watch the sunset turn the dunes red, before dinner.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Depart; short drive up the Dades gorge (about 30 min).
10:30 – Walk in the Todra Gorge (about 1 hour).
13:00 – Lunch in Tinghir or Tinejdad (not included).
15:00 – Fossil workshop in Erfoud (optional, about 30 min).
16:30 – Arrival at your hotel with pool at the foot of the dunes.
18:30 – Sunset over the Erg Chebbi; dinner.

GOOD TO KNOW
• About 280 km and 5–6 hours with stops – a gentler day.
• Buying fossils is entirely optional.
• The pool is usually open from April to October.

INCLUDED: private 4x4 and driver, hotel with pool, dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

PHOTO SPOTS
• The Dades hairpins from the viewpoint café.
• The narrowest part of the Todra in morning light.
• The dunes at sunset from the hotel terrace.

Overnight: hotel with pool at the foot of the Erg Chebbi.
Meals: breakfast, dinner.

What to expect: a private day exploring the desert by 4x4, a rest by the pool, then a sunset camel ride to your luxury camp for dinner under the stars.

After a relaxed breakfast your driver takes you around the Erg Chebbi in the 4x4. The route depends on the season and your interests, but usually includes a nomad family's tent for tea and bread baked in the sand, the village of Khamlia where descendants of West African families play Gnawa music, the seasonal lake of Dayet Srji (with flamingos in wet winters), old fossil and mineral sites on the hamada, and viewpoints over the highest dunes. Lunch is wherever you like, often a Berber pizza (madfouna) in Merzouga.

In the afternoon you return to the hotel to rest and pack a small bag. At around 17:00 your camels are waiting at the edge of the dunes. The ride into the sand takes about an hour as the light turns gold. At the camp, your tent has a king-size or twin beds, linen, rugs and its own bathroom with hot shower. Dinner is served by candlelight or under the sky – soup, salads, a tagine and dessert – followed by drums around the fire and, on clear nights, the Milky Way.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:30 – Private 4x4 tour around the dunes, nomad tea and Khamlia music (about 4 hours).
13:30 – Lunch in Merzouga (not included).
15:00 – Rest at the hotel and pool.
17:00 – Camel ride to the luxury camp (about 1 hour).
18:30 – Sunset from the dunes; sandboarding if you wish.
19:30 – Dinner under the stars, music by the fire.

GOOD TO KNOW
• If you prefer not to ride, you can walk or be driven to the camp by 4x4.
• Camps have electricity for lights and charging phones; bring a power bank to be safe.
• Some luxury camps serve wine; ask us in advance.

INCLUDED: private 4x4 tour, camel ride, luxury tent with en-suite bathroom, dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

PHOTO SPOTS
• Camel shadows on the dunes at sunset.
• The lantern-lit camp after dark.
• The Milky Way over the dunes.

Overnight: luxury desert camp in the Erg Chebbi.
Meals: breakfast, dinner.

What to expect: sunrise over the Sahara, breakfast at the camp, and the long road back to Marrakech by a different route through Rissani and Ouarzazate.

Wake up before dawn and climb the dune behind the camp to watch the sun rise over the Erg Chebbi – one of the most memorable moments of the trip. After breakfast in the camp you return to Merzouga by camel or 4x4 and set off west. You pass Rissani, the historic heart of the Tafilalet near the ruins of the caravan city of Sijilmassa, then take the southern road via Alnif and N'Kob or the faster road back via Tinghir, depending on time.

After lunch, the road crosses Ouarzazate and climbs over the Tizi n'Tichka once more before descending to Marrakech in the evening.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
06:00 – Sunrise over the dunes.
07:30 – Breakfast at the camp.
08:30 – Depart Merzouga.
09:15 – Rissani.
13:00 – Lunch on the way (not included).
15:00 – Ouarzazate.
17:00 – Tizi n'Tichka pass.
19:30 – Arrive in Marrakech.

GOOD TO KNOW
• This is the longest day: about 560 km and 10–11 hours with stops.
• To avoid it, we can add a night in Ouarzazate or Skoura, or end the tour in Fes instead (about 7–8 hours).
• Morning flights out of Marrakech on Day 4 are not possible; plan your flight for the next day.

INCLUDED: private 4x4 and driver, bottled water, drop-off at your riad or hotel.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, tips.

WHAT YOU TAKE AWAY: the Sahara without compromise – two nights at the dunes, real comfort and the time to enjoy them.

faq.question: What is a luxury camp?
faq.answer: A camp of large tents in the dunes, each with a king-size or twin beds, quality linen, rugs, electric light and an en-suite bathroom with hot shower and flush toilet. Food and service are a step above standard camps.

faq.question: Is it private?
faq.answer: Yes. You travel in a 4x4 with your own driver, with no other guests, and can set your own pace.

faq.question: Which meals are included?
faq.answer: Dinner and breakfast each night. Lunches are not included so you can choose where and how much to eat.

faq.question: Is it suitable for honeymooners?
faq.answer: Yes. Tell us when booking and we can arrange touches such as a private dinner setting, flowers or a cake at the camp.

faq.question: Why two nights at Merzouga?
faq.answer: It gives you a full day to explore the desert by 4x4 and rest by the pool, instead of arriving tired at the camp after a long drive and leaving at dawn.

faq.question: How long is the drive back to Marrakech?
faq.answer: About 560 km and 10–11 hours with stops. If you prefer, we can add a night on the way or end the tour in Fes, which is closer.

faq.question: Is there electricity and Wi-Fi at the camp?
faq.answer: There is electricity for lights and charging. Wi-Fi is limited or absent in most camps, which many guests enjoy; mobile data often works on the dunes.

faq.question: Do I have to ride a camel?
faq.answer: No. The ride is about an hour and suits most people, but you can walk or be driven to the camp by 4x4 instead.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the camels, sandboarding and the nomad visit, and the comfortable rooms and pool make it easier for families. Child seats are available.

faq.question: When is the best time to go?
faq.answer: March to May and late September to November are ideal. Summer is very hot in the day; December to February is sunny but cold at night.

faq.question: Can we end the tour in Fes?
faq.answer: Yes. Day 4 can finish in Fes instead of Marrakech, with a drive of about 7–8 hours through the Ziz valley and the Middle Atlas cedar forests.

faq.question: Is alcohol available?
faq.answer: Some luxury camps and hotels serve wine and beer; others do not. Tell us if it matters and we will choose accordingly.

faq.question: What should I pack?
faq.answer: A warm layer for nights, swimwear for the pool, a scarf and sunglasses, sunscreen, comfortable shoes and a small bag for the camp night.
